models_evaluated: FDA-cleared intracranial hemorrhage AI detection overlay

links.outcome: Self-reported reduced scrutiny after AI-negative result and conditional trust in AI output
links.effect: Reduced scrutiny after AI-negative result reported by 4/65 (6.2%; 95% CI 2.4%-14.8%); 50.8% trusted AI when it agreed with their read vs 3.1% when it conflicted.
links.quote: Self-reported reduced scrutiny after an AI-negative result was uncommon (4/65, 6.2%; 95% CI 2.4%-14.8%).

links.outcome: Perceived false-positive burden and time savings from AI in radiology workflow
links.effect: Only 10.8% (7/65) reported reduced overall interpretation time; 33.8% (22/65) agreed false-positive review time outweighed benefits; 18.5% found false-positive alerts acceptably infrequent.
links.quote: Only 10.8% (7/65; 95% CI 5.3%-20.6%) reported reduced overall interpretation time, whereas 33.8% (22/65; 95% CI 23.5%-46.0%) agreed that time spent reviewing false-positive alerts outweighed the benefits.

screen.reason: The study surveys radiologists actively using an FDA-cleared ICH AI tool in real-world teleradiology practice to assess perceptions, trust, false-positive burden, and workflow impact, but does not test a specific deployment practice intervention.
